## A
## A

Aaron is interpreted as “mountain of strength,” 1598. Aaron was a figure of Christ, ibid. Aaron resisted the wrath of God when he took the censer and stood between the dead and the living, 299. Aaron is commanded to wear twelve stones on his breast when he enters the tabernacle, 899, 1503. Why Aaron is called holy in Psalm 105:16, 1385. What Aaron and Hur, who supported Moses’ weary hands, signify, 1598.

Abel did not resist his brother who was killing him, 132. The blood of Christ speaks better than the blood of Abel, 426. He prefigured Christ’s Passion, 948. Abel offers us an example of patience and humility, 1338. He refuses to be Abel whom Cain’s wickedness does not exercise, 673, 1259, 1638.

The fir signifies men in the Church who contemplate heavenly things, 1523. Abigail signifies discernment in interpreting her husband Nabal, 1286.

To deny oneself: what this means, 1083. Let us deny ourselves as we made ourselves by sinning, and remain as we were made by grace, 1587.

The holy Fathers born before the time of redemption are called abortions, 132. By recounting only a few, Moses concealed from us the greatest part of the human race, ibid. Those who have been withheld from our knowledge are called abortions, ibid.

[Col. 1343] Abraham’s humility in considering himself ashes even while speaking with God, 97, 1242. Abraham proceeding to meet the angels while Sarah remained in the tent: what this signifies, 336. Abraham teaches us obedience, 860, 1338. While Abraham was a pilgrim in the world, he became God’s friend, 132. Why he buried his wife in a double tomb, 207. Abraham driving the birds away from the sacrifice: what this signifies, 521. Abraham questioned with difficult commands, 898. When he saw the day of the Lord and rejoiced, 1508. He had two sons of different character, 673. Why, after receiving three angels, he spoke as though to one, 1508. What it means for sons to be raised up for Abraham from stones, 1520. The bosom of Abraham: what it is, 1653. Who calls the rich glutton Abraham’s son, 1654.

**To hide.** The saints hide themselves before the face of God, mortified by the cares of tumultuous affairs, 142. The righteous have hidden God’s words in their bosom, 517. Men customarily hide their sins, 712. Through repentance the sinner hides himself from God, 116. God sometimes hides himself from the elect, 191, 513, 550. The hidden Word is the Son of God, 160. The breathing of the Holy Spirit is also called the hidden Word, 161.

Who are said to be drunk with wormwood, 222, 654.

**To absolve.** The presider’s absolution is true when the judgment of the inner judge follows it, [Col. 1344] 1555. The order of priestly absolution, 1556. He who frees a dead man displays not virtue but stench, ibid. “Let the disciples loose him” as he comes forth, 1556.

Men who abstain are signified by the name of the wild ass, 982. Simon of Cyrene signifies those who abstain and those who are arrogant, 1589. Those who abstain do not hear the cry of the exactor, 982. The abstinence of hypocrites is empty, 277. The wicked abstinence of heretics who detest foods, 504. Abstinence must be moderated by discernment, 675. By the blows of our abstinence we strike not the air but unclean spirits, 982. What the abstaining boys unharmed by the Babylonian fire signify, 983. What must be eaten is what necessity demands, not what desire suggests, 983. How much discernment is necessary in abstinence, 675, 983. To dig the earth with the hoof means to subdue the flesh by strict abstinence, 1031. What kind of abstinence is a snare of guilt, 1238. Abstinence is signified by the name of the tambourine, ibid. Vain glory besieges abstinence from the flesh nearby, 1588. What good abstinence produces, 982. What false abstinence is, 1238. Through abstinence the vices of the flesh, not the flesh itself, must be extinguished, 675. See **Gluttony**.

The abundance of possessions draws the mind away from God, 19. Abundance is censured, [Col. 1345] 490. Who knows how to abound? 1386. Abundance is near pride. See **Riches**.

The abyss signifies the human heart, 588; the human mind, 929; hell, 927; the incomprehensible judgments of God, 1132. To call upon the abyss means to proceed from judgment to judgment, 875. What it means for the devil to be bound in the abyss, 588. What it means for God to walk in the farthest reaches of the abyss, 929. What it means to constrain the face of the abyss, 947. What it means for the abyss to grow old, 1132.

The error of the Academics and Mathematicians is refuted, 1088. “To receive” sometimes means the same as “to take away,” 1091. What the hawk signifies, 1001, 1013, 1038. What it means for the hawk to grow feathered in the south, 1037. Certain noteworthy things about the hawk, ibid.

What it means to recline between boundaries, 25.

**To accuse.** He who accuses himself and rages against his own injustice is righteous, 1234.

What vinegar in soda signifies, 1262.

Ahab is called reprobate, 1280. His repentance pleased God, ibid. Ahab was worthy of being deceived according to the demands of his merits, 54.

The battle line of the camps is called the Church, 1237. It is packed with charity so that it may become terrifying, 1238.

Fiery battle-lines seen in heaven in the time of Saint Gregory, 1436.

For a good action to be more worthy, it ought to appear unworthy to the agent himself, 146. Someone is often believed to possess a certain merit whose baseness is exposed in every action, 193. The action of this world is compared with a millstone, 193. Action precedes contemplation, 209. The actions of the flesh come first in the hearts of the reprobate, 639. The quality, form, and extent of a good action must be examined, 1111. An action must be examined at the root of its intention, 1224. Good and evil actions should be hidden, 1449. The recompense of good and evil actions is carried out with the utmost strictness, 1656. See **Work, works; Active and contemplative life; Contemplation**.

Humility is signified by the eye of a needle, 1160.

Adam is called the first man, 788. Adam is interpreted as “red earth,” 592. Adam was a man, not “the son of man,” 540. Adam is corruption, whose sons are called worms, ibid. Adam’s sleep signifies silence of mind, 981. He is called “day” by reason of his creation and “darkness” by reason of his fall, 1163. See **Names of man**.

Adam was created on the day of justice, 106. Before the fall, by what merit Adam would have attained blessedness, 126. When Adam could stand, he did not wish to, 250. He possessed contemplation of the inner light, 387. He could have conquered the enemy without difficulty, 1164. By his very creation he received the good of salvation, 1164. See **The state of man before sin; The state of innocence**.

Adam was created so that he could be without sin and without death, 126. While he stood, times passed, 391, 788. When the first humans desired the likeness of divinity, they lost the gifts of immortality, 604. Man fell because he wished to be like God through power, not through righteousness, 925. Adam had two sons, one elect and the other reprobate, 673, 1638.

Adam resisted the command of the Creator and was cast down, 290. The free man brought death upon himself through food; brought back to pardon and enclosed under discipline, he lives better, 327. Why the first parents, but not the serpent, were questioned after the guilt, 712. The devil tempts human beings every day in the manner in which he tempted the first parents, [Col. 1345] 765. Those whom guilt then led to punishment, punishment now recalls from guilt, 765. The devil inflicted the wound of pride on the healthy man, 995. The first parents wrongly used the shield of excuse, 1106. Adam was struck by a threefold temptation, 1493.

Adam lost the power not to sin, having voluntarily subjected himself to the enemy, 126. If it becomes known what we have lost, it will be clear how serious is what we endure, 213. How great the weakness of the human soul after the fall is, 244, 268. The instability of fallen man, 250. When man believed that he was sufficient for himself, having abandoned God, he found only disturbance, 269. By sinning he incurred the punishment of both deaths, 306. The mind is continually driven toward what is worse by the weight of its mutability, 391. Adam became bold after the guilt, 123. Adam hid himself after sin, 712. He excused his sin through the woman, ibid. Why the Lord rebuked fallen Adam while walking, 895. Having lost heavenly riches, he fell into the poverty of the present life, 1117. Adam was expelled from paradise because he followed his own will, 1156. Adam’s weakness after being recalled from the fall by God, 1163. And strengthened by the helps of grace, ibid. Adam needs greater helps after the fall than before it, 1164. We need many virtues that would not have been necessary in paradise, ibid.

After Adam’s sin, the flesh resists the spirit, 126. Man could have possessed the flesh in tranquility if, once well created, he had wished to be possessed by his Creator, 244. The sentence written concerning the death of sinful man remains immutable, 387. Man, created for life, made himself of his own will a debtor to death, 552. Man did not wish to persevere in the righteousness he had received from the Creator, 765. The life of man after sin is a passage; before sin it was otherwise, 788. Why Adam covered his nakedness after sin, 824. Adam, unwilling to be subject to God, became subject to the flesh, ibid.

In Adam, as in a root, mankind was corrupted, 543. If Adam had not sinned, he would not have generated sons of Gehenna, 131. Of Adam’s two sons, one was elect and the other reprobate, 673, 1638. Since the condemnation of the first man was transmitted to his descendants, let them beware lest they add their own sins, 311. Many imitate Adam by covering their sins, 712. This guilt of concealing sin has grown exceedingly, 713. See **Original sin; The state of fallen nature**.

What the diamond signifies, 1270. The adamantine nail signifies the eternal end, 460. Fat signifies pride, 494.

To wish to help the weak is charity; to help the powerful is pride, 545. In what sense we are said to help God, 545. The proud do not wish to be God’s helpers, ibid.

Youth signifies newness of life, 763. Youth is the womb of evil thought, 915. In Scripture “youth” sometimes means the age of young manhood, 1184. The third hour signifies youth, 1511. Youth is suited to good works, 388. The sins of youth must be mourned, 1599.

By the grace of adoption we are called God’s offspring, 656. We received the grace of heavenly adoption through Christ, 730.

Who is truly said to adore God, 71. An angel is adored by man in the Old Testament, but in the New Testament he is forbidden to be adored, 866, 1462.

Flatterers are said to bury their dead, 125. The tongues of flatterers are of no benefit to hypocrites at the judgment, 472. How harmful it is to flatter sinners, 559. The tongue of a flatterer is expressed by the name of the locust, 1018. The tongues of flatterers devastate the fruits of good works, [Col. 1346] ibid. Flattery must be extinguished immediately, 1286. Flattering speech is fire, 1413. A loud voice is the utterance of a flatterer’s favor, ibid. It subtly creeps into the mind, ibid. Flatterers are sellers of oil, 1478. The sinner’s oil fattens the head when the favor of the flatterer caresses the mind, 1478. The tongue of flatterers is signified by the tongue of a licking dog, 1653.

Spiritual adultery is represented by the likeness of carnal adultery, 528. What it means to adulterate the word of God, 529, 716. Adultery is committed by sight alone, 687. The difference between adultery and fornication, ibid. Both are forbidden, ibid. Heresy is compared with adultery, 528.

Christ’s first coming was in humility; his second will be in terror, 555. The coming and dwelling of divine wisdom in human hearts are unknown, 606. Before Christ’s coming, even the righteous descended to the inner places, 668. Sacred Scripture easily passes from the first coming to Christ’s second coming, 1189. The splendor of the Judge at the second coming will allow no sinner to remain hidden, ibid. Who loves Christ’s coming, 1421. See **The Last Judgment; Christ’s Incarnation; Nativity**.

Adversity is signified by night, 44, 114, 432. Adversity tests friends, 223, and exposes enemies, 224. Who makes good use of prosperity or adversity, 172, 1386. Adversity becomes prosperity for the righteous, by which they are made safe from vanity, 251, 851. In adversity the wicked accuse God, 271. God sometimes mercifully inflicts adversity, 382. God must be regarded in adverse circumstances, 518. Adversity does not strike down the joyful righteous person but increases his grief, 513. He who acts rightly and endures adversity labors in adversity but will be perfected in glory, 531. Many placed in adversity do not believe that God exists, 557. The wicked, oppressed by adversity, secretly harm the good by crooked counsels, 528. Adversity does not overthrow the one whom prosperity does not corrupt, 668. Adversities must be endured outwardly with courage and inwardly with gentleness, 710. He who desires no prosperity fears no adversity, 717. Adversity reveals whatever virtue or weakness lay hidden in us, 758. The benefits of adversities, 865, 947. Adversity increases virtue, 1022. See **God’s scourges; The effects of scourges; Prosperity; Tribulation; The saints in adversity; Affliction**, etc.

Why the word of God is called “the adversary,” 329, 1648. How we are delivered from this adversary, ibid. How one ought to conduct oneself in the struggle against adversaries, 1023. Adversaries can be called helpers, 1616. See **Enemy, adversary**.

A righteous advocate does not undertake unjust causes, 1234.

**To build.** One must destroy before building, 564. What a spiritual building is like, 1311. The breadth of the spiritual building is charity, 1327. Its height is understanding of the Creator, 1328. The walls of the building are the less perfect, 1333. What the outer and inner thresholds signify, 1335. The façades of the heavenly building are called the holy Fathers of both Testaments, 1346. They are also called the outward works of the virtues, 1359. Without faith, hope, and charity there is no access to the heavenly building, 1360. Holy Church, that is, the spiritual building, has only three doors by which it reaches secret joys, 1384. The Church is built with square stones, the Jews having fallen, 1406. The difference between the construction of the heavenly building and that of an earthly one, 1630. The breadth of the heavenly building is as great as its height, 1328. Its courtyard [Col. 1347] is the vastness of faithful peoples, 1426. See **Courtyard; Door; Church; Heaven**.

Illness presses longer because the vices are more prolonged, 1515. Just as the wishes of desperately ill people are not denied, so they are not denied to the reprobate, 681. Who among the faithful should lay hands on the sick, and how they should fare well, 1571.

Egypt signifies the present life, 820. What has oppressed us while flattering us may help us while pressing us, ibid.

The remarkable conversion of the monk Aemilianus, 1610. Aemiliana, Saint Gregory’s aunt, a virgin devoted to good works, 1642. Aemiliana’s blessed passing, 1643.

Air is called heaven, 66. Air is ordered according to the quality of heaven, 127. In relation to heaven, air is called hell, 435. The minds of worldly men are signified by air, 885.

Bronze signifies the insensitive hearts of human beings, 222, and perseverance, 1124. Resonant bronze is one who does not follow what he says is good, 1063. Glowing bronze is preaching set aflame, 1194. What the sparks proceeding from glowing bronze signify, ibid.

No one ought to consider himself possessed of any virtue, 760.

Heat signifies persecution, 935. What it means to bear the burden and heat of the day, 1512.

The ages of man are various, 388. Just as the ages of the body are various, so are those of the mind, ibid. The world has its ages, like human beings, 1115, 1510, 1511. As the world grows old, its tribulations increase, 1115. In each age one must keep watch as in as many watches of the night, 1483. The different ages of man or of the world are signified by different hours of the day, 1510, 1511. Our age remains vigorous until old age and afterward declines daily, 1115. Mature age is required in a preacher, 1184.

Eternity measured by years, 857. Temporal things, compared with eternal things, are narrow and contemptible, 133, 236, 391. He who desires eternal things grows weary from love of temporal things, 134, 264, 393, 496, 985, 1279. Our place is eternal light, 134. Beginning or perfect love of eternal things diminishes and kills envy, 180. He who yearns for eternal things fears nothing from the world, 356. The brief life is followed, according to merits, either by blessed or miserable eternity, 402. Eternity must be in our intention, temporality in our use, 489, 1320. He who asks with his mouth but does not desire eternal life with his heart is silent while crying out, 718. What eternal light is, 777. Certain things will be eternal, although they have not been eternal, 857.

The reprobate, deceived by the devil, do not believe in the eternity of punishments, [Col. 1347] 1132. The eternity of punishments and rewards is established, 1132. The perfection of eternity is signified by the number seven, 1150. Eternal things are before us; temporal things are behind us, 1198. To pant after eternal things is to walk before one’s own face, ibid. Eternal things have no savor for those who love earthly things, 1263. The anguish of the soul hastening toward eternal things but slipping back toward the depths under the weight of mortality, 1318. After the narrowness of the present life comes the breadth of eternity, 1341. Why the day of eternity is called the eighth day, 1341. We give a portion to seven and also to eight when we arrange temporal things so as to reach eternal things, 1342. We reach these through a double charity, ibid. Those who love eternity possess all temporal things for use, not for affection, 1387. Present things must be ordered with consideration of eternal things, 1649.

Eternity has neither past nor future, 127, 521, 666, 1508. We learn eternal things with difficulty; we quickly forget them, 268. Eternity sees past and future things as present, 321. He who desires eternity is not disturbed by present things, 356. The conditions of eternity, 521. Those awaiting the rewards of eternity draw strength from adversities, 821. See **God’s eternity; Time; Temporal things**.

What Ethiopia signifies, 597.

How the affections become capable of meriting heavenly things, 665. Those who succumb to carnal affection are called beasts of burden, 766.

Affliction draws man back from sin, 259, 516. Here affliction is certain, but how long it will last is uncertain, 17. Affliction drives away vices, 99. The usefulness of the afflictions of this life, 211. By God’s excellent counsel we are afflicted here, lest we love the way instead of the homeland, 754. The afflicted learn to sympathize with the affliction of others, 419. Afflictions are necessary in this life, 424. The wicked do not believe that the good are afflicted in this world, 469, 512. Affliction purifies from sin and increases merits, 516. It belongs to an afflicted heart to ask God about things unknown to it, 747. Moderate affliction draws out tears; immoderate affliction suppresses them, 330. The place of affliction is the present life, 663. The varieties of the afflicted, 557, 558. See **Adversity; Tribulation; Scourge**.

Agabus’s prophecy, 1157. He who acts deceptively sins, even if he offers rightly, 82. We must consider not only what we do but also with how much discernment we act, 83. Everything done here is punishment and misery, 192. Through what is done outwardly, whatever lies hidden within is revealed, 495. See **To act; Works**.

What the field signifies, 524. The world is signified by a field, 1003, 1076, 1488. What it means to cultivate one’s field with prepared labor, 351.

Saint Agnes’s encomium, 1473. How great the shame that her courage brings upon us, ibid.

Who the Agnoite heretics are, 27. Saint Gregory gave them no support, 28.

**Lamb.** The distinction between lambs and kids at the judgment, 383. What it means to eat the lamb, 645. What it signifies to consume the remainder of it in the fire, ibid. The ewe offered for sin signifies the innocence of the active life, 148. What it means to eat the lamb in one house, 1148. Who it is that dwells with the lamb as a wolf, 1342. We learn the blood of the Lamb not merely by hearing but by drinking, 1533. What is placed upon both doorposts, ibid. Who are on the lintels of the houses, 1534. What it means to eat the flesh of the lamb roasted by fire at night, ibid. What the unleavened bread and wild lettuces signify, ibid. The flesh of the lamb must be eaten neither raw nor cooked in water, but with the highest reverence toward Christ God, 1535. What it means to devour the lamb’s head with its feet and entrails, ibid. When by understanding and doing all God’s commandments we penetrate everything, nothing of the lamb remains until morning, ibid. What it means to have one’s loins girded while eating the lamb, ibid. What it means to have sandals on one’s feet, 1536. Why those eating the lamb are commanded to gird their loins before taking up their staffs, ibid. See **Passover**.

The prophet Ahijah’s harsh words to Jeroboam’s wife, 1177. Ahijah’s mind was touched by the spirit of prophecy with regard both to the present and to the future, ibid.

What spiritual wings are, 769, 1235, 1274. What the two wings signify, 1202, 1233. What it means to strike one another with wings, 769. What God’s wings signify, 1050. What the wings of the living creatures signify, 1144, 1233, 1274. What it means to lay down the wings, 1144, 1241, 1242. What the two wings with which the body is covered signify, 1233. What the sound of the wings signifies, [Col. 1348] 1235. To strike one wing against another is to rouse one virtue by means of another, 1274.

In what way the righteous regard the sins of others, 98. What it means for each person to pass over what is alien, 407. An apostate angel is called alien, ibid., 1118.

Allegory builds up faith; history, morality, 1652.

What the Philistines who filled the wells dug by Isaac signify, 509, 1021.

What it means for the earth gradually to be consumed by inundation, 401.

What it means to make an altar of earth for God, 93. The bloodless sacrifice of the altar, 710. The altar of God is the mind of those who live well, 1427. What the two altars of the tabernacle signify, 1428.

The origin of the word *altilia*, 1636. Why *altilia* signify the Fathers of the New Testament, 1636. Who are the bulls and the slaughtered *altilia*, ibid.

The elevation of mind that looks upon invisible and eternal things, 236. What the heights of the earth are, 1040. Height is the promise of the heavenly kingdom, 1220. The height of the saints is faith in invisible things, 1409.

Amalekite is interpreted as “the licking people,” 1622. What “the licking people” signifies, ibid. The Egyptian boy left sick on the road by his Amalekite master: what this signifies, 173, 1622. What David striking down the feasting Amalekites with the sword signifies, 1622.

The highest and lowest things cannot simultaneously and equally be loved, 564. No one can love what he does not believe, 1348. Against the lovers of this age, 630. See **To love**.

Bitter and sweet together, 1280. What it means to write bitter things for God, 387. What the bitterness of the wise is, 587, 1279. What it signifies to impose bitterness upon oneself, 1034. He becomes bitter to himself for whom God is sweet, 1280.

Ambitions are innumerable evils, 786. Two kinds of men serve their ambition, 649.

What it means to walk in emptiness, 230. What it signifies to walk in the way of vineyards, 531. To walk before the face, 1198. Before the face, 1204.

Friends are sometimes called adversaries, 98. How great the injustice of despising a friend in adversity is, 224. A friend is recognized in adversity, 223. A friend is, as it were, the guardian of the soul, 1562. Wounds inflicted by friends are more grievous, 1614. A friend in God, and an enemy for God’s sake, must be loved, 1466, 1560, 1640. He calls someone a friend and rejects him because he was a friend by faith but not a friend by works, 1641. See **Friends of Christ**.

Love often rouses sluggish minds to work, 208. Punishment asks whether someone truly loves while at rest, 10. What is possessed with love is not lost without grief, 19, 1006. The power of love is the mind’s mechanism, 209. Knowledge is the measure of love, 1409. To love higher things is to go upward, 490. The force of love, 1548. The proof of love is the presentation of a work, 1575. Love is never idle, 1576. True love, once it has filled the mind, torments it with tears, 1578. Love is a flame, 1606. Inner love sometimes conquers the pain of the flesh, 1445. The power of love multiplies the search, 1546. See **Love, affection**.

He who, out of love for God, has begun not to will to sin has completely withdrawn from evil, 29. See **Contrition; Conversion**. Because of love for God, the adversary fears to speak wickedly to the grieving person, 94. The more we are strengthened in the love of God, the more we fall away from our own power, 134. The soul fears and loves God the more deeply as it is raised higher into God, 162. Our hearts are badly healed when they are wounded by no love of God, 200. It is better to love God as a father than slavishly to fear him as Lord, 217. We love God more firmly when, for God’s sake, we more usefully neglect ourselves and our own, 232. By love alone we render God the services due for his gifts, 318. The love of God produces weariness of life, 318. We kindle the sacrifice when we burn with the fire of divine love, 326. The divine word, commanding that God be loved, indicates not only from what source but also with how much love he should be loved, 340. One must return from penal fear to love, 387. When man lost the love of the Creator, he lost the warmth of his heart, 390. Hearts empty of divine love are possessed by the devil, 547. Love of God and love of the world cannot be contained in one heart, 563. How great is God’s love for us, since he does not abandon us even when he is rejected by us, 957. Love teaches one to speak sweetly of God, 1267. One does not reach the love of God unless faith is held first, 1348. Insofar as each person loves, so far does he draw near to entering heaven, 1360. We must be suspended in the love of God and joined to our neighbor in charity, 1379. Faith and life must be maintained in the love of God, 1404. Charity toward God cannot be perfect here, 1409. Here charity is called fire; in heaven, a furnace, ibid. The love of God is the title of divine possession, 1544. The effects of divine love, 1547, 1574. The rust of guilt is burned away by this fire of love, 1547. Love itself is knowledge, 1562. Proofs of divine love, 1574. Whoever loves God already possesses him, 1575. The proof of love is the presentation of a work, ibid. How great is the dignity of one who has God dwelling within, 1576. Life must be questioned about the love of God, ibid. The manner of loving God is to love without measure, 1639. See **Charity; Love**.

Christ did not wish to be feared as God but wished to be loved by us as a father, 317. Christ kindles angels through his divinity and righteous human beings through his humanity with the fire of love, 1247. How carefully Christ must be sought, 1546. What it means to seek Christ by night, ibid.

Patience and kindness must accompany love toward one’s neighbors, 241, 1404. If either is absent, there is no love, 242. Each person should think of and love himself in another, 205, 1205. Love of neighbor takes care not to harm and is concerned to do good, 340. In how many ways these two commandments are fulfilled, 341. The righteous seek in everything not only their own progress but also the edification of their neighbor, 383. The wicked, by living badly, cannot be merciful toward another through compassion, 624. Without charity there are no good works, 643. He who has lost the eye of love does not see where he is placing the foot of a good work, 695. By distributing his gifts to the wise, God safeguards charity and humility, 904. Love of neighbor is proved not by the tongue but by works, 1355. Through the practice of good works the mind expands into love of neighbor, 1379. Exhortation to love of neighbor, 1581. With what discernment we ought to love and hate parents and relatives, 1623. He who loves his neighbor hates him in the same manner as he hates his own soul, ibid. The measure of love of neighbor, 1639. Love of neighbor is reduced to two commandments, 340.

What the love of God and the love of neighbor render to each other, 223. The love of God and neighbor is signified by the two wings with which the bodies of the living creatures are covered, 1233. It is also signified by twice-dyed scarlet, 1501, 1640. There are two commandments of charity, 1554, 1640. In the love of neighbor the love of God is learned, 1554. Neither is God truly loved without one’s neighbor, nor is one’s neighbor truly loved without God, [Col. 1349] 1581. Some burn with such love of God and neighbor that they are rightly called Cherubim, 1607. We must be suspended in the love of God and joined to our neighbor in charity, 1379. Charity toward one’s neighbor can be perfect; toward God, it cannot, 1409.

Disordered love of relatives brings one back to the snares of the world, 231. For God’s sake we ought to despise relatives, though we must not know how to hate them, 231. We ought to benefit relatives more than others, provided that our progress toward God is preserved, 232. Holy men, through their love of spiritual things, overcome within themselves even the love of relatives, ibid. The mind must be neither harsh nor lax toward relatives, so that it may bend more when touched, ibid.

What a jar lifted between heaven and earth signifies, 462.

What is signified by the blossom of the almond tree, 1017.

Ananehel is interpreted as “the grace of God,” 798.

What is called *anathema* among the Hebrews is called *alienatio* (“alienation”) among the Latins, 682.

The anchor of the heart is the weight of fear, 208.

The Lord bound Leviathan by means of his maidservants, 1095. What the maidservants sent by Wisdom signify, 1096. Preachers are called maidservants through fear, friends through faith, and merchants through action, ibid.

How quickly the apostle Andrew was converted to Christ, 1450. We celebrate his feast as we ought by imitating what we venerate, 1453. Following the example of Saint Andrew, the saints exchange temporal things for eternal things, ibid. Whoever is not yet able to abandon his own possessions should at least not covet those of others, 1453.

**Forced service.** Things done under compulsion for the sake of good are fruitless, 277. The citizens of Jerusalem sometimes pay forced service to Babylon, 589.

*Angel* in Greek means “messenger” in Latin, 1455, 1547, 1604. The word “angels” is the name of an office, not of a nature, 1604. The elect angels are called sons of God, 39. They are called kings, 127; consuls, ibid.; princes of the nations, 541; soldiers of God, 542; days and months, in a certain sense, 109.

Angels are called the pillars of heaven, 550; refined gold, 590; morning stars, and why, 909; precipitous flints, 1041; inaccessible rocks, ibid.; the beauty and ornament of God, 1051. The angels of the churches of Asia are preachers to the peoples, 1122. The waters in heaven are called the ranks of angels, by which the higher regions of heaven are covered, 1353. The ninety-nine sheep signify angels, 1601. The nine orders of angels are compared with nine precious stones, 1604. The names of the chief angels are explained, ibid.
