Original sin is abolished through baptism, 313. Heaven was closed to the righteous of the Old Testament because of original sin, 433. We draw original sin from our parents, 491, 598, 761. Once original sin has been erased, children are no longer held liable for their parents’ wickedness, 492. From where the weakness of the guilt of the first sin is propagated in human offspring, 543. From original sin arises the restless mutability of man, 849. The sin of the first parents, 1658. No human being is without sin except the one conceived without sin, 1350, 1649. He is the one Redeemer of the Church, ibid., 1649.

Actual mortal sin is completed through four stages in the heart and through an equal number in deed, 123. These four stages are signified by the death and burial of Lazarus after four days, 125. The habit of sinning sometimes precedes the blindness of the mind and sometimes follows it, 229. The two principal sins are pride and vainglory, 461. Whether sin is committed in faith or in deed, one does not escape the vengeance of divine condemnation, 532. What is the sin unto death? ibid. Many are without crime, but no one is without sin, 688. We feel sins to be more grievous in proportion to the greater love of our heavenly homeland with which we are affected, 839. Through a hidden disposition of God, the evil that is done is not permitted to remain unknown, 875. The seven capital sins arise from pride, together with their daughters, 1035, 1036, etc. The two carnal and five spiritual sins, ibid. [Col. 1457]

Venial actual sin. We slide from lesser offenses into more serious ones, 349. The righteous punish lesser offenses in themselves with great torments, 382. With what vigilance the saints guard against even lesser sins, 385. Small sins are forgiven those who have sternly lamented greater sins in themselves, 484. Those whom great sins oppress are likewise afflicted by lesser ones in hell, 485. No saint is without sin in this life, 543, 590, 688. Some sins can be avoided by the righteous, others cannot, 561. Whoever defends evil deeds adds sin to sin, 119. Sin is perpetrated in four ways, 123. Likewise in three ways, 145, 803, 1064. Sin arises from sin, 227. Sin is perpetrated in two ways, 351. First there is guilt in thought, then in deed, 443. To think perverse things is to sin, 561. To sin knowingly is to descend alive into hell, 565. How grievously those sin who seek impunity for sin through their ignorance, 803. One thing is to sin through weakness, another through malice, 1007. In falls one begins with the least and reaches the more serious, 1009. When crime is defended, it increases, 1080.

While the soul is fed by sin, it cannot eat the bread of righteousness, 382. Teeth bound by the habit of sin cannot eat the just thing that they taste within, ibid. No human being is free from sins of thought, 385. Through sin man is led to ignorance of himself, 386. No one is without sin except the one who did not come into the world from sin, 396, 1579. The harsh captivity of sin—how it may be recognized, 440. We can flee not the temptation of sin but its dominion, 443. So that we may be God’s inheritance, sin must not reign in us, 680. Guilt is punished by guilt, so that punishments increase with the growth of vices, 799. The necessity of sinning contracted through habit, 1064. Sins are so entangled that, while one is avoided, we almost always fall into another, 1065, 1203. In a case of perplexity, the lesser sin should be chosen, 1067. Every sin is serious, 1185. Many sins that we commit never seem serious to us, 1204. Sin drives out all former good, 1289.

How the righteous should regard the sins of others, 98. A man’s sin magnified by his excuse, 119. The first virtue is to avoid sins, 199. The abuse of sins, 245. By sinning man has become contrary to God, 267. The weakness of the flesh excuses man, 323. Why man after sin merited forgiveness from God, ibid. We are crushed by wound upon wound when we add sin to sin, 425. For those who sin through ignorance and weakness, God is present as our illumination and salvation, 451. All sins must be avoided completely, 621. Man wishes his sin to be hidden from God, 712. It is more difficult to expose committed sins than to avoid uncommitted ones, 714. Whoever is placed in sin forgets his mortality, 783. The easier one escapes from sin, the less one is constrained by habit, 843. No one is excused from sins against the law of nature, 875. Why some neglect to put an end to their sins, 1132. Why we judge our own serious sins lightly and the light sins of others severely, 1204. What it means to eat sins, 1499. The perfect should always lament their past sins, 1400. No one should despair of a neighbor enslaved to sins, 1514. The sinner is wholly bent over by the habit of sinning, 1585.

Why the angel’s sin is unforgivable, 322. See Angel: Sin.

God leaves no sin unpunished, [Col. 1458] 117, 349, 826. God punishes man through those things that, in sinning, he preferred to his Creator, 79. Let us leave none of our sins unpunished, 119. When we leave our sins unpunished, we are possessed by night, 118. When we punish our sins through repentance, we shall possess night, ibid. Whoever detects the deceiver’s snares punishes his own sins, 120. The second virtue is to correct sins that have been committed, 199. The opposition of guilt has become a burden of punishment for man, 268. The punishments of the first sin, 269. The delight of sin is brief, its punishment eternal, 225. Who knows the vanity of men and considers their iniquity? 349. Hidden sins are to be corrected secretly, and public sins publicly, 420. What are the scourges of sin? 429. What sins of parents do children bear? 491. Through original sin, not washed away in baptism, a son bears the iniquity of his father, ibid. For a perverse mind its own guilt becomes punishment, 479. After the fall, the eyes of the wicked are opened uselessly, 492, 493. Why adult children are punished for their father’s sin, 492. The wicked will rise to be tormented both in body and in soul, 508. Sin not erased by repentance leads even to hell, 532. No sin is hidden from divine wrath, 547. Whether anyone is scourged twice for the same sin, 572. While just vengeance removes the unjust, it restrains others from wickedness, ibid. The greater crimes of men should be believed more slowly and, once truly known, punished more quickly, 628. Those struck by God for instruction are freed from sin, 669. Whoever is scourged for his sin without complaint has already begun to be righteous, 746. Every sinner passes from this corruption of vices to the sword of punishments, 753. Sin not quickly wiped away by repentance is sin and the cause of sin, or the punishment of sin, 799, 1289. Those entangled in sins cannot see the light, which they did not wish to see when they could, 801. In the bosom of the Church, those living wickedly are struck by divine vengeance as though they were impious, ibid. How grievously those sin who seek impunity for sin through their ignorance, 803. Hidden sins are punished publicly by God, 824. Which sins God begins to strike in this life and completes through eternal condemnation, 829. Why some sins are struck by the Lord here and others are reserved unpunished, ibid. Crimes increase in proportion as they are tolerated unpunished through the defense of the powerful, 1080. God pursues sins but protects sinners, 1182. Sins that could be struck by the fires of hell are to be corrected by the rod of discipline, 1381. Whoever willingly endured the darkness of pleasure here suffers the darkness of vengeance, 1466. The punishment of sin is not to refrain from evil though one knows it and [has received] a gift, 1585. In everything we have sinned; in everything we are struck, 1613. Calamities arise not from the injustice of the one who strikes but from the merit of the world that suffers, ibid. Punishment binds those whom guilt has bound away from good works, 1641. Those who corrupt the memory of sins once erased and renew the battle, 325.

Sins must be confessed, but excuses must not be made, lest they be doubled, 119. The love of God brings one to confessing errors, 318. Confession must be made in bitterness of soul, 319. In sacred Scripture confession is signified by the name “pledge,” 502. By excusing sins, we make them more serious, 712, 1106. The beginning of illumination is the humility of confession, 713. The sinner comes out of the tomb through confession, ibid. Confession of sin without humility is feigned, ibid. The signs of sincere confession, ibid. To confess sins is often more difficult than to avoid them, [Col. 1459] 714. Some wish to adorn themselves through confession of sin, not to humble themselves, 770. A devout confession is a voice powerful in God’s ears, 841. The debtor’s pledge is the sinner’s confession, 502, 1091. Confession of sins is the opening of wounds, 1652. When the holy teachers instruct us in the confession of sin, they touch the wound of the mind through the tongue, 1653.

The medicine of sin is the humility of lamentation, 91. The fourth stage of sin—that is, the boldness of defending it—is more difficult to cure, 125. Whether there is no memory of sin in heaven, 138. Sin is driven from the mind by fear, followed by love, from which a resolve is also conceived, 29. Sins are forgiven through repentance, 213. Either a person punishes sin within himself through repentance, or God strikes it in vengeance, 313. From correction and our repentance we gain confidence in forgiveness, 324. The Church teaches that sins are cleansed through voluntary affliction, 425. What is the sin unto death and the unforgivable sin? 532. Guilt accompanied by piety is easily wiped away, 559. There is no remission of sins outside the unity of the Church, 574. What it means for sins to be covered, 1203. The physician’s power is greater than the magnitude of our sickness, 1264. When sin is not quickly erased by repentance, the punishment is often a subsequent sin, 1289. The crowd that waited three days for the Lord signifies the faithful’s repentance for their sins, 1416. Who come from far away to the Lord through repentance, 1417. The rust of sin is consumed by the fire of love, 1595. See Repentance.

Money enclosed in a purse is hidden wisdom, 1498. Who are the feet of the Lord? 578, 615. What it means to wash one’s feet with butter, ibid. The feet of the Church are the lower ministers, 616. Feet signify the course of actions, 1193, 1536. Whose feet are straight? 1193. What it means for the feet and hands of the reprobate to be bound, 1641. What it means to place a foot on an ox and an ass, 1161. What it means for the devil’s snare to be hidden in the earth, 441. The error of the Pelagians, who trust that they can be saved by their own powers, 1054. Pelagius and Celestius are refuted as enemies of grace, 1158. What it means to give skin for skin, 75. What the skins and sackcloths with which the tabernacle is covered signify, 809. What the goatskins with which naked Jacob is covered signify, 1214.

What is the way of penetrating heavenly and spiritual things? 627. What the wings of animals joined one to another signify, 949, 1198. What it means that God flew over the wings of the winds, 549, 606. What it signifies to cast off an old feather and take up a new one, 1038. A feather expresses flight, 1191. It also signifies contemplation, 1192. Who are called four wings of each of the four animals? 1193. What are the four wings of the saints? 1203. What it means to extend or lower wings from above, 1202. The two wings directed toward the future are love and hope; toward the past, fear and repentance, 1203, 1233. Likewise, love of God and neighbor is signified by two wings, ibid. What the straight wings of the animals, one joined to another, signify, 1232. What is a wing in Ezekiel is received grace in Peter, 1232. See Wing.

The feast of Pentecost is compared with the feast of the Incarnation of the Word, 1580. How honorable is the solemnity of Pentecost? ibid. The wallet signifies the burdens of the world, 1498. The various kinds of blows, 12. A divine blow is called a disturbance, 75. God strikes the elect in two ways, 200. A blow sometimes comes from God, sometimes from the adversary, 219. A divine blow is the purification of the present life or the beginning of a punishment to come, 571. God’s blow is a father’s discipline, 696. Heavenly striking is expressed by the name “hammer,” 1125. See Scourge.

Some lose what they seemed to possess; others receive what others lose, 796. Consolation in the loss of possessions, 51. The sign of perdition is when the affection that follows favors the iniquities one has desired, 827. All the saints are pilgrims in the world, 577. How great are the sorrows of this pilgrimage? ibid. The saints are pierced by weariness of this pilgrimage and love of their heavenly homeland, 1428. Pilgrims are to be compelled to come into lodging, 1538.

The perfect person does not lose humility by observing another’s fault, 98. Our perfection is not free from fault if it is examined by God without indulgence, 148. Perfection is born from patience, 153. The perfect person is one who is not impatient with his neighbor’s imperfection, ibid. No one here is so perfect that something needing to be cut away does not continually arise in him, 165. By what means the summit of perfection is reached, 209. Perfection is signified by the number one thousand, 289, 723, 1162. Likewise by the number seven, 22, 1149, 1150, 1162, 1543. The effort of striving toward perfection, 517. It belongs to the perfect to grieve the losses of the weak as their own, 612. Various stages toward perfection, 720, 1329. The perfect grieve more over the losses of others in proportion as they grieve less over their own, 725. God’s indulgence toward beginners, 1030. All the perfect will sit judging with Christ, 1190. Those who lament their own faults and offer their neighbors examples of virtue are perfect, 1234. Let the little ones imitate the tears and virtues of the perfect, ibid. No one suddenly becomes supreme, 1329. Perfect minds are signified by apples from the flowers, 1332. Who should be called perfect? 1373. Perfect men are compared with Ezekiel’s animals, 1190, 1201, 1223. With what effort one must strive toward perfection, 1382. Those entangled in worldly cares are not free for perfection, 1383. The ardor of a mind panting after perfection, ibid. How far many are from perfection, although they flatter themselves that they have attained it, 1383. Nevertheless they will attain it if they humble themselves according to their weakness, 1384. The perfection of virtue is signified by the eighth degree, 1392. The perfect should mourn the sins of their former way of life, 1400. For whom their imperfection is not harmful, 1515. God judges perfection one way and human beings another, 1660.

“To perish” is used in two ways, 106. The kings of the Persians come forth from the lineage, 1470. The threshing of persecution awakens the ardor of virtue that lay hidden, 10. What is the disposition of a poor person oppressed by persecution for God’s sake? 235. The persecutions of the Gentiles must be broken by the power of miracles, 293. Persecution is stirred up in two ways, 611. The tribulation of the final persecution, 664. In unjust persecutions one must have recourse to the heavenly judgment, 812. The persecutions of the impious instruct the good, 820. The raging storm washes the elect but does not submerge them, 910. The storm of persecution either leaps forth or is quieted by divine judgment, 912. Wicked Christians who are not tempted appear to bear the seal, but when truly tempted they are clay, 922. As persecution increased, so did the ardor of the apostles and holy preachers, [Col. 1460] 938. Persecution is expressed by the name “sun,” 1126. Whoever in peacetime sluggishly fails to subdue the desires of the flesh would not, in persecution, bravely undergo death for God, 1473. In time of persecution the soul must be surrendered; in time of peace evil desires must be broken, 1589. The usefulness of persecution, ibid. When persecution has ceased, how can we test our faith in Christ? 1590. The savage persecution of Antichrist, 446. See Antichrist; Temptation.

Our persecutors are those who entice us to evil by words or examples, 88. Those who persecute the saints are called their friends, 458. Who is a good persecutor and who a wicked persecutor? 459. The wicked persecutor’s evil will, which God uses well, ibid. Against the words of detractors, wisdom is necessary; against the swords of persecutors, patience, 557. The perverse persecute the works of the good with mockery, 651. The persecutors of the Church are perverse and numerous, 664. God moderates the wrath of persecutors according to his dispensation, 911. As the life of the faithful became brighter, the cruelty of the faithless was kindled, 935. Those who were formerly persecutors of the faith later became its preachers and defenders, 998. Our persecutors are swifter than the eagles of heaven, 1038. Those by whom we are oppressed are to be loved as brothers, 1618. Persecutors are to be punished in soul and body with eternal torments, 1637. The memory of the persecutors perished, ibid.

Perseverance is necessary, 38, 703, 1207. The one who acts rightly does not know whether he will persevere, 143. The hypocrite does not persevere in good works, 274. To preserve what we are, we must always weigh what we were, 903. Whether anyone will persevere either in righteousness or in sin is hidden from us, 931. The usefulness of this ignorance, 932. Perseverance is signified by the name “air,” 1124. The perfect day signifies perseverance, 1207. Rocky soil receiving the seed of the word signifies lack of perseverance, 1490. Perseverance is the virtue of a good work, 1546. Perseverance is signified by the tail of the sacrificial victim that is to be offered, ibid. And by the long robe of the patriarch Joseph, ibid. Whoever knows what he is today does not know what he will be tomorrow, 1643. This is established by the examples of Gordiana and a certain Theodore, 1645.

There is no partiality with God, 787. The shaking of the final disturbance, 1189. In inward disturbance one must have recourse to the Lord, 72. The perverse attack the life of the good in two ways, 152. The perverse sometimes speak well of the righteous, ibid. The perverse sow and reap sorrows, 154. In a perverse mind the dragon lies and the ostrich feeds—what does this mean? 228. We love doing perverse things but condemn them when seen in others, 233, 1205. It belongs to a perverse mind to reject both the correct and the incorrect statements of opponents, 287. The perverse habitually accuse the good of the evils of which they themselves are guilty, 417. What is the place of the perverse? 571. The perverse love tribulations for the glory of this world, 654. When authority is given to the perverse, the door of error is opened, 662. The perverse occupy a place of honor among the reprobate, so that they may rage against the Church from a position of authority, 674. The perverse do not walk before their own face, 1205. The perverse scorn to be God’s dwelling place, 1272.

Why God delays the voices of those who ask, 665. Those who ask proudly do not receive because they ask wrongly, 691. What we ought to ask from God, [Col. 1461] 1563. See Prayer; Prayers.

The rock is called Christ, 96, 616, 1040, 1554. Who is called the rock, a refuge for hedgehogs? 985, 1261. What it means that we are commanded to enter the rock, 1021. Rocks in the plural are the exalted powers of heavenly virtues, 1041. Holy men, who are members of Christ, are also signified by the name “rocks,” 1040. What it means to ascend the rock, 1149. Why Peter was called “Satan” by Christ, 89. In what way Peter was a door, 912.

Peter the elder signifies the Church, 1531.

Peter understood no other wisdom of God than what there was, 595. Peter’s eminence, 1368. As a future shepherd of the Church, Peter learned from his own fault to show mercy, 1527. The Church was specially entrusted to Peter, 1542. Peter displayed the solidity of eternal peace to the faithful through words, letters, and miracles, ibid. Peter was superior to Paul, 342. Peter’s virtue grew by degrees to perfect strength, 721. Peter showed himself superior to human sins, but equal to human beings, 833. Peter and the other apostles, made solid by grace from air into clouds, 885. In Peter’s example a measure of authority and humility is proposed, 906. The Church’s door was opened to Cornelius and closed to Simon, 912. After his fall Peter is raised by Christ to hope of forgiveness, 1527. Therefore he is called by name by the angel, ibid. Peter signifies the Church of the Gentiles, just as John signifies the Synagogue of the Jews, 1531.

Before Christ’s death and resurrection Peter retained a carnal mind, 89. Peter is rebuked because he tries to fix the tabernacles on earth, 287. Peter, first of heaven—that is, of the apostles—denied life when he feared death, 553, 1579. How useful Peter’s fall was, 773. Peter sinned through weakness, 803. Peter, wishing to undergo the danger of the Passion, nevertheless refused it, 1028, 1445. At Antioch Peter had fallen into hypocrisy, a more serious fault, 1367. Whom Peter signifies when, as a sinner, he repels the Lord from himself, 1465. Why Peter was permitted to fall, 1527. Leviathan held Peter in its mouth, from which he escaped through the opening of repentance, 1551. God gave us Peter as an example of repentance, ibid. The marvelous courage of Peter, formerly weak and fearful, 1579.

Peter fearlessly addresses the rulers of the Jews, 237. Peter’s mercy, ibid. How great his courage was after receiving the Holy Spirit, 553. Peter, previously prostrate at the voice of the doorkeeper, presses down the strength of rulers after being struck, 554, 1339. How discerning Peter was in the exercise of power, 833, 834. Peter did not delay punishing Ananias and Sapphira for their fault, 833, 1228, 1368. Peter, when Cornelius humbled himself, refused to be honored excessively, 833. What is more devout than Peter? 859. Peter did not fear to announce the word of God because of threats from superiors, 906. Peter heard Paul’s counsel concerning the Gentiles not being circumcised, ibid. His authority and humility, ibid. After healing the lame man, Peter went like a flash of lightning, but returned, giving praise to God, the author of the work, 958, 1212. Christ receives the repentance infused into Peter by himself, 1235. Peter admired Paul’s wisdom, and Paul admired Peter’s innocence, 1276. Peter grew by stages of virtue, 1331. By his example Peter teaches us to lay down our life for God and to rejoice amid scourges, 1339. Peter praised the inferior who rebuked him, 1368. First at the summit of the apostolate, he is first in humility, ibid. He forgets all his gifts so that he may remember his one humility, ibid. Those who say that this is another Peter, not the apostle, are refuted, ibid. Peter’s zeal and patience, 1228, 1339. Peter’s bitter weeping, accepted by Christ, 1235. How great Peter’s gentleness was, 1368. Peter’s supreme humility, ibid. Those who deny the apostle Peter his Second Epistle are refuted, 1369. Peter was washed in the fountain of mercy by bitter weeping, 1402. The first shepherd of the Church lived neither for himself nor died for himself, 1425. Peter, by refusing the torture of martyrdom, came to desire it, 1445. How promptly Peter followed Christ, 1450. How much he left behind, ibid. He who first feared words later did not fear blows, 1580. The Holy Spirit fills the fisherman and makes him a preacher, ibid.

In his Epistles Peter asserts that Paul is worthy of admiration, 1368. What Peter’s and John’s running to the Lord’s tomb signifies, 1530. Peter, arriving later but entering first, signifies the Church of the Gentiles, which came later but believed in Christ first, 1531. Peter and the other apostles returned without fault after their conversion to the lawful occupation of fishing, 1540. Why Peter’s net was full of fish, 1542.

Why Pharaoh’s vision through a dream was not prophecy, 378. That Pharaoh’s heart was hardened by God, 1008, 1291. What a closed quiver signifies, and what an open one, 658. What the quiver signifies in sacred Scripture, 1025. After the sound of the quiver, the spear is brandished, 1026, 1033. The Pharisee justified himself in deed, 406. The Pharisees detested Christ, 457. The Pharisee lost his good works because they were not protected against exaltation, 621, 1225. The pride and condemnation of the Pharisees, 622. The Pharisee had an eye for giving thanks to God but not for humility, 1225. The Pharisees’ arrogance at Mary’s conversion, 1594. What the bowls and cups used for the tabernacle signify, 636, 1455. What it means to pour a bowl into the sun, 1127. The Philistines guarding Samson after capturing him in Gaza signify the Jews placing guards at Christ’s tomb, 1529. In what the true philosophy of God consists, 49. Whether philosophers who followed the natural law could have been saved without a mediator, 592. Phinehas teaches us zeal for uprightness, 1338. He resisted God’s wrath when he appeased the fury of divine indignation with the sword, 299, 1339. The wicked, rejoicing in evils, are like the frenzied, 193.

Painting. In painting, black color is laid underneath, 1094. Heavenly piety first acts in us without us, 512. See Prevenient Grace. God’s long-suffering and piety are to be imitated by us, 517. Christ gave us the form of piety, and Paul taught it, 670. Piety toward the poor is the companion of humility, 692. See Almsgiving; Poor. The perfection of piety, 1380. Piety without the gift of knowledge is disordered, 1381. What true piety is, and what false piety, 1589. How great Christ’s piety toward sinners is, 1597.

A pledge signifies two things in sacred Scripture, 502. What it means for the lazy to pass through a field, 662. Who considers it labor to raise his hand to his mouth because he is lazy? 1411. What the Levites’ hair, which was to be shaved and not plucked out, signifies, 165. What the goats’ hair offered for the service of the tabernacle denotes, 967. Who are called hairy ones? 228. The harshness of every sin is signified by the hairy ones, ibid. What it means for “the hairy one” to call to “the hairy one,” [Col. 1462] ibid.

God subjected orators to fishermen, 1098. The Lord is read to have commanded fishing twice, 1541. What it signifies that fishing was commanded to be done on the right side, 1542. Fish with fins customarily leap over the waters, 146. The curious fish of the sea …

[They] signify this age, 368. What the gathering of every kind of fish within the net signifies, 1474. The 153 fish caught in the nets: what they signify, 1543. The roasted fish: what it signifies, ibid. Why honeycomb is eaten with roasted fish, ibid. Why the fish without fins were excluded by the law from the food of the faithful, 1586. What the finned fish signify, ibid.

No one pleases God through fear, 385. One who pleases God and displeases human beings has no cause for sadness, 485. The person to whom God has begun to be pleasing displeases himself, 1279. Wounds in the innermost parts of the belly: what they are, 750. To plant and water is to help, 545. The first planting is from God, the second from human beings, 395. See *Prevenient grace*. *Plateia* [“street”] is used for breadth, 1071, 1503. Who are said to proceed through the streets and not to be known in the streets, 1071. The stones of the sanctuary are scattered in the streets when religious people pursue the broad roads of the world, 1504.

How the people of God become contemptible, 757. Plaits signify unanimity in concord, 1414. The Pleiades: what they are and what they signify, 948, 950. The sheet of lead: what it signifies, 460. Lead signifies greed, ibid. Rain signifies the preaching of the word of God, 295, 609, 636, 881, 941. The stars that send forth rain: what they are, 857. Why God is called the father of rain, 941. Rain signifies grace, ibid. Voluntary rain: what it signifies, ibid. Why the Lord is said to rain upon one city and not upon another, 1272.

The uses of the punishments of this life are manifold, 12. The evil of punishment comes from God, 51, 79, 367. The saints are strengthened against fear of punishments by the nourishment of the word of God, 202. Punishments are signified by the name of arrows, 214. The punishment of the first sin, 252. Why God takes delight in our punishments, 307. Present punishment does not always assure future glory, 319. Present punishment frees from eternal punishment only those whom it changes, ibid., 491. What it means for punishments to wage war within us, 329. The punishments of hell are neither temporary nor imaginary, but solid and everlasting, 331. The punishment of demons and condemned human beings is the same, 332. Different degrees of the same punishment, ibid. Those whom a similar guilt stains are bound by an equal punishment, 333. Human punishment arising from sin is twofold, 390. Misery is born from our punishment, ibid. Evils often befall the good, 438. Eternal punishment presses upon the one who is exalted here by temporal glory, 439. One who abandons justice through fear of punishments does not escape the punishments he fears, 453. Present punishment does not free from eternal punishment when it does not convert the soul of the wicked, 491. What we should fear in the punishment of others, 572. Punishment questions us whether we truly acknowledge our guilt, 770. Punishment will open the eyes that guilt closed, 790. The two punishments of the wicked, 799. The wicked do not recognize their guilt except in punishment, 796. Because punishment is delayed, guilt is despised, ibid. The evils of present punishment are light compared with those of the future, 1099.

Repentance is a second baptism, 1471. The treasure in the field is hope in [Col. 1463] repentance, 35. The dungheap signifies the hearts of the penitent, 87. Only the penitent finds a place in which to hide from God the judge, 116. Healthy sorrow arising from wrongful pleasure, 117. What it means to be wrapped in the bitterness of repentance for a day, 118. Through repentance freedom from sin is acquired, 137. From where the tears of repentance, even among the saints, proceed, 145. One is ashamed of the labor undertaken for love of the present life when recalled from error, 249. The sorrowful despise present things and await future things, 250. The confession of sins ought to be accompanied by the mourning of repentance, 258. How many things the bitterness of repentance discloses to the mind as needing to be mourned, 259. God delays punishing, giving room for repentance, 370, 506, 1479. When God abandons someone, repentance is either absent or false, ibid. The righteous do not know how to spare their own faults, so that God may spare them, 383, 400, 401. Through repentance the first robe is recovered, 396. Unless sins are washed away by repentance, they will leave the secret storehouse and emerge into the public judgment, 400. Confidence of the soul cleansed through repentance, 510. Repentance is to mourn past evils and not to commit again what ought to be mourned, ibid., 1609. The fruit of repentance among the righteous, 514. The time given to a sinner for repentance becomes punishment when neglected by him, 537. The repentance of some is feigned, 770. Late repentance is described as indeed late, but nevertheless true, 871. The objects of repentance are neglected goods and committed evils, 1047. In his vengeance the penitent joins himself to God and rises up against himself, 1049. What it means to practice repentance in dust and ashes, 1146. What is to be considered in the sackcloth and ashes of repentance, ibid. Sacred Scripture pierces readers with compunction toward repentance, 1229. We ought to attend to our neighbor in such a way that we never forget to mourn our own sins, 1233. Fear and repentance are signified by the two wings with which the bodies of the animals are covered, ibid. The repentance of little ones: what it is, 1234. The sinner’s repentance is signified by the shaken earth, 1273. A quarrel arises in the soul as it gives birth to peace with God, 1280. Even the repentance of the reprobate pleases God; how much more that of the elect, ibid. Exhortation to repentance, 1402, 1443, 1525, 1552. Repentance proportionate to the gravity and number of sins, 1520. Repentance is signified by the opening in Leviathan’s jaw through which those whom he has bitten escape from his mouth, 1551. Divine medicine meets us everywhere, ibid. God has given us examples of repentance in those whom, after their fall, he enabled to live through repentance, ibid. When the Lord willingly accepts our repentance, he hides by his judgment what we have done in error, 1570. The sinful woman who comes to Christ gives us the pattern of repentance, 1595. The manner of repentance, 1609. Whoever has done unlawful things should abstain from lawful ones, ibid. The long-suffering of God as he awaits our repentance, 1610. Exhortation to repentance, with the example of a certain repentant Victorinus, 1611.

Late repentance of the reprobate, 874. Late repentance is useless, 1479. Repentance must precede absolution, 1555. God does not seek what has been forgiven through repentance, 115. The beginning of pleasure must be chastened by the laments of repentance, ibid. How powerful repentance is, ibid. The coming judge will not bring against us what we have pursued through repentance, 116, 119. We either pursue sin by weeping or God pursues it by vengeance, 117. While the soul is affected by the groaning of repentance, it is filled by the refreshment of divine consolation, 144. The force of the bitterness of repentance, 258. The bitterness of repentance extinguishes eternal punishments, 319. How great is the [Col. 1463] necessity of repentance for sins already forgiven, 325. How much the repentance of the righteous avails to stir the wicked to repentance, 382. Repentance to be performed in secret for sins of thought, 385. A sin that is not corrected by repentance before death becomes unforgivable, 532. God saves some through innocence and others through repentance, 574. Through repentance God rescues us from corruption and afterward from the sword of divine judgment, 753. From the mourning of the penitent arise the virtues of the saints, 1274. Before the merciful judge, the very recognition of guilt will command pardon, 1283. The sinner who abuses the time of repentance turns the remedy of grace into an increase of guilt, 1291. True repentance equals the merit of innocence, 1380. Involuntary movements toward vice must be chastened by the tears of repentance, 1400. What repentance is necessary for sinners, and how much of it, 1443. Whoever has lost the appropriate time for repentance will cry out in vain for the closed door of the kingdom to be opened to him, 1479. Whoever promised forgiveness to the penitent did not promise the sinner tomorrow, ibid. Not repentance alone, but worthy fruits of repentance are required, 1519. The punishment of those who do not bear worthy fruits of repentance, 1520. What we did not hold during life, let us seize through repentance as the inheritance of the righteous, 1525. How great is the power of repentance, 1525, 1551. Repentance restores lost innocence, 396. At the final judgment, sins hidden by repentance will not be illumined by the light of vengeance, 116. To possess the night, or to be possessed by the night, signifies the effect or failure of repentance, 118. From the voluntary punishment of repentance follows a certain security of the soul, 319. The bitterness of present repentance extinguishes the punishments of the coming wrath, ibid. The righteous punish lighter offenses in themselves with great torments, 382. What the effects of repentance are, 867. Let us abandon and accuse our evils, and the just advocate will not defend us in judgment, 1234. Through the laments of repentance one reaches the song of life, 1264. Hearts that were receptacles of demons become a dwelling-place of the Lord’s glory through repentance, 1274. The effect of true repentance, 1380. Whoever urges sinners to repentance has taught that the kingdom of heaven is seized by force, 1525. By what acts of repentance a certain Victorinus obtained from God forgiveness of his crime, 1611. The twofold groaning of repentance, 1048. Through repentance one virtue arouses another, 1275. What the manner of repentance is, 137, 1009.

The beginning of repentance, 385, 386. The healthy darkness of the repentant mind, 117. How great the bitterness should be for consent to guilt, 118. Confession with bitterness, 319. Through repentance the justice once lost is often recovered more strongly, 452. External discipline washes away faults; the compunction of repentance pierces the mind with the vengeance, 751. The wounds of blows cause pain; the laments of compunction are sweet, ibid. Through the repentance of conversion we ought to anticipate the divine judgment, 792. The twofold groaning of repentance is signified by two young doves, 1048. The useful disturbance of repentance, 1273. The times of repentance must not be neglected, 1575.

Repentance for hidden sins, 325. Repentance in ashes and sackcloth: what it is, 1146. The repentance of little ones, 1234. The raising of Lazarus after four days demonstrates the order of priestly absolution, 1555. He is called by the Lord and brought to life, but is released by the disciples, 1556. Whoever releases the dead displays not power but [Col. 1464] stench, ibid. The giving of life is shown in spontaneous confession of sin, ibid. The necessity of this confession, ibid. Conscience must first be examined and disturbed in preparation for repentance, 1603. Through repentance we return to God, 1471.

The penitent sighs before eating, 144. The care of the penitent, 250. The slow destruction of penitents, 789. God promised forgiveness to the penitent, but not tomorrow to the penitent, 1479. We ought to sympathize with penitents, 1594. Torpor toward repentance is rebuked, 1402. Most people begin to repent but immediately return to their customary ways, 414. What it means to repent, 666. The manner of truly repenting, 771, 792. Whoever regrets having done something corrects what he did, 1243. Heaven is open not only to the innocent but also to the penitent, 1382. In good works, penitents are sometimes more eager than the innocent, 1385. How a priest ought to conduct himself toward a penitent, 1594. How sweet the tears of the penitent are as a feast for Christ, 1597. The fervor of the penitent pleases God more than the righteous person’s sluggishness in good works, 1562. There are righteous people with whom God rejoices more than with penitents, ibid. The example of a true penitent, 1611.

The pollution of a menstruating woman is the soul becoming filthy through depraved thought, 1401. What it signifies that germinating fruits are unclean, 280. What the fruits of paradise signify, 310. Ships carrying fruits: what they are, 309, 310. Self-love has a double weight and a double weight, 1205. The double burden of merchants, ibid. What the absolution of a murderer by the death of the supreme pontiff signifies, 1218. The people of the Church are called an orphan, 241, 620. Peoples signified by water, 546, 550, 607, 943, 956, 1235. The pilgrim people are the number of the elect, 577. Unskilled peoples are designated by the name of flocks, 522.

The gate signifies Christ, 183, 1327, 1329, 1331, 1397, 1422. What it means to sit in the gate, 617, 693. The gate of the city: what it signifies, ibid. The gates of death are wicked actions, 617. Likewise, hostile powers, 928. The gates of Zion are good actions, 617. Likewise, the gates of Zion signify holy men, 1103. In the gate of the city judgments were formerly rendered by elders, 693. The gates of Leviathan’s face are false preachers, 1103. These are open for admitting but closed for detecting, ibid. What it means for Christ to stand at the gate, 1316. What it means to look toward the gate, 1317. By looking toward the gate we turn our backs on the present life, 1318. What is signified by the name “gates,” 1329, 1355. The gate is Christ, whose threshold is the holy patriarchs, 1331, 1335. The front of the gate: what it signifies, 1342. The front of the gate is measured by two cubits, that is, by love of God and neighbor, ibid. What the breadth of the gate’s threshold and the length of the gate signify, 1346. The narrow gate that leads to life, 900, 906, 1536. The narrow gate, which …, ibid. The narrow gate becomes broad for those who love, 1359. The gate facing the north: what it signifies, 1377. The gate toward the east and the gate toward the north: what they signify, 1380. Why the gate of the spiritual building toward the East is called faith, 1384, 1421. Hope is toward the North, ibid. Charity is the gate toward the South, 1385. Through the eastern gate the Lord, through the southern gate Judea, and through the northern gate converted Gentile peoples are signified, 1397. The inner gate is the Church, which leads us to inner joys, 1419. What the vestibule of the city gate, measured by two cubits [Col. 1465], signifies, 1640. By the name “gates” holy preachers are understood, 1329, 1403. Likewise sacred Scripture, ibid., 1346. Likewise faith, 1353.

What it means to carry the world, 300. The stone is carried in the building and carries, 1311. Let the one who is carried learn to carry, ibid. Christ, the foundation stone, carries everyone and is carried by no one, ibid. What it means to possess goods, 490. What disposition we have toward the things we possess, we do not know until they are lost, 1006. Whatever is possessed without love is lost without pain, ibid. God’s right of possession in us is recognized from the person of our possessor, 1545.

The Lord wishes eternal things to be requested rather than earthly things, 489. True petition lies not in words of the mouth but in the thoughts of the heart, 718. What it means to ask for the Holy Spirit, 1576.

What the powerful ought to be toward their subjects, 145. Those who cling to an unjust powerful person swell with his power, 411. Arrogant powerful people exist in the Church like dishonorable members in a body, 420. Temporal power, even when good, is exposed to the temptation of pride, 832, 833. A powerful ruler has a horn, but it is bound by the cord of divine fear, 998. The proud power of the wicked is signified by the name of the cedar, 1058. The wicked powerful are called the bones of Antichrist, and those who cling to them are called his flesh, 1063. How much temporal power is worth in merit before God, 832. The powerful are forbidden to become inflated, 833. Power must be used carefully, ibid. How praiseworthy is the humility of the powerful, 835. God grants power, but our wickedness invents the pride of power, ibid.

How power ought to be used, 146. Those placed in power often lose what is useful, 146. What dangers beset those placed in power, ibid. Whoever can exercise power well, 833. The dangers of temporal power, ibid., 835. Power ought to be pressed inwardly in proportion as it stands out outwardly, 834. The freedom of the saints, outwardly oppressed, in reproving the powers, 236. This freedom arises from zeal for truth, not from the vice of pride, 237. Whoever sees that he can do more than others easily believes that he knows more, 832. Legitimate power is not over human beings but over human faults, 833. The remarkable harmony between secular power and Christian humility, 997. Christ entrusted his Church to earthly power, 999. Earthly power is signified by the voice of the eagle, 1038. The swelling of secular powers is expressed by mountains, 1076. Those who ascend the mountains and those who descend into the valleys, ibid. Why powers are called a certain order of angels, 1605. What the office of the heavenly powers is, ibid.

What drink signifies, 26. What it means to temper the Lord’s drink with weeping, 797. How bitter drink gives pleasure for the sake of health, 1028. The wicked consider nothing right except what they themselves have perceived, 337. The wicked join remembrance to their own calamity, 649.

Why commandments were given to human beings by God, 9. To keep the commandments of the Decalogue is great joy, 447. As many commandments as Christ gave the Church, so many kisses, 455. Many righteous people add the evangelical counsels to the Lord’s commandments, 477. Those who do not obey God’s commands drive him away from themselves, 488. Those who disregard God’s commandments ask the Lord and are not heard, 510. The heart condemns the one who hears the divine commandments but does not perform them, 560. What it means to feign grief over a [Col. 1465] commandment, 571. Whoever meditates on God’s commandments has God dwelling within him, 613. Which commandments of the old law are called “not good,” 913. When we conceive the divine commandments, we do not immediately give birth, 975. The commandments of the Church are the reins of discipline, 997. They keep God’s commandments by singing, working not from fear but from love, 1420. God’s commandments are called justifications, 1230, 1420. God gives us life in his commandments, ibid. All God’s commandments must be esteemed highly, 1263. Great commandments were given on the mountain, lesser ones in the valleys, 1293. The divine commandments are in sacred Scripture, 1337. Whoever preaches by voice what he does not keep in his life dissolves the commandment and teaches, 1476. The divine commandments were received through the Decalogue, 1494. God’s commandments are compared with women’s mirrors, 1501. The Lord’s commandments are both many and one, 1560. Christ gave new commandments, 1586. The commandments of the New Testament are not easier than those of the old, 1654. The commandments of the New Testament are more subtle than those of the old law, 1658. Different commandments are given to those lying down and to those standing, 1250. We must first fulfill God’s commandments so that we may properly teach our neighbors, 1270. To do good because of a commandment belongs to beginners; to do it from charity belongs to the perfect, 1274. Some commandments are higher, others lesser, 1396. By keeping the commandments we offer sacrifice, 1404. The Lord’s two disciples are illumined not by hearing but by carrying out the commandments, 1538. God gave human beings commandments so that they would not sin, and remedies for sinners so that they would not despair, 1551.

The prey that the devil promises his companions, 430. What it means to snatch prey from the devil’s teeth, 628. Why predestination is called God’s womb, 456. An example of gratuitous predestination in the thief who obtained salvation, 586. Whatever will occur outwardly in action has already occurred inwardly in predestination, 900, 1273. Many among the wicked who were foreknown and predestined are called in their own time to great things, 934. Predestination and reprobation are unsearchable and incomprehensible, 943, 953. No one can understand or know his own predestination, 953. Human beings predestined to occupy the seats deserted by apostate angels, 1041.

The manner of preaching used by the arrogant, 778. Likewise, the manner of preaching used by the righteous, ibid. What the holy preachers ought to preach, 881. God chose the weak for preaching, 1096. Why Christ did not wish to preach before the age of thirty, 1185. Young men ought not to preach, 1183, 1184. The Law, the Prophets, the Gospel, and the Apostles preach the same thing, 1218. To preserve the truth of preaching, the height of one’s life must necessarily be maintained, 1284. Christ, by a hidden judgment, commands some to preach and forbids others, 1316. Whoever becomes Christ’s brother or sister by believing becomes his mother by preaching, 1444. Those who preach for the sake of praise or payment deprive themselves of eternal reward, 1499.

Preaching is signified by arrows, 213. It is likewise signified by neighing, 1016; by the name of rain, 295; and by the name of water, 371. It is foretold that the preaching of God’s word will be transferred from the Jews to the Gentiles, 290, 292. Preaching is the root of the righteous person, 394. Preaching flowed to the Gentiles after the Jews were abandoned, 578. The streams of oil are the preaching of the apostles, 616. There are two modes of preaching: one by words, the other by deeds, 675. God strengthened the force of preaching amid the straits of persecutions, 938. At times preaching drips like dew, [Col. 1466] and at times it pours abundantly like rain, 942. What the work of preaching is, 1096. Holy preaching is called by the name of a sword, 1122; likewise by the name of a spear, 1123; and by the name of iron, ibid. Holy preaching does not drive Satan away from the hearts of the reprobate, 1124. The words of preachers are signified by the name of arrows, ibid. It must be feared that those who speak about God may either say evil things carelessly or fail to say good things well, 1168. What it means to speak good things well, ibid. Sacred Scripture kindles readers’ zeal for the work of preaching, 1229. The word of preaching is seed in the heart of the hearer, 1194. The authority of preaching given to the prophet, 1253. What circumstances of preaching must be observed, 1286. Preaching taken from the Jews will return to them from the Gentiles, 1294. In what way God grants or withdraws from preachers the gift of speaking, 1298. Christ’s preaching from the flesh is like sound from air, 1314. The preaching of the Law is carnal; that of the Gospel is spiritual, ibid. Subtle preaching is signified by the name of a linen cord, 1315. The Jews envy the preaching made to the Gentiles, 1596.

The preaching of the word, rejected by the Jews, was transferred to the Gentiles, 61. When preaching is withdrawn, the heart withers, 371. A preacher must consider the capacity of the hearer, 549. Preaching must cease when hearers become worse because of it, 658. The reprobate try to extinguish the life of faith and the voice of preaching in the Church, 664. Those subject to vices ought not to devote themselves to preaching, 741. Holy preachings will cease with the present life, 874. The more the divine word is worn down, the more its power increases, 926. The light of preaching shone widely through the voices of the apostles, 935. The wicked must be rebuked with loud and powerful voices, 962. Fiery preaching is signified by glowing bronze, 1194. The authority of one who admonishes should be humble if he is superior, and free humility if he is inferior, 1253. The fruit of evangelical preaching, 1235. What effects preaching has in the mind of the weak, 1319. As the perversity of the wicked increases, preaching must not be abandoned but increased, 1508. Christ continued to preach the truth to the Jews who resisted him, ibid. From the beginning to the end of the world, God sends preachers to instruct the faithful, 1510.

The person who sends ahead the seeds of good action gathers abundant fruits of preaching, 206. Words proceeding from a cold heart cannot inflame hearers, 277. External preaching is useless when God abandons the hearer’s mind, 370, 345. Many hear admonitions in order to judge them, not to follow them, 469. The irrigation of preaching, like a torrent, divides the good from the wicked, 577. In the stony hearts of the Gentiles God opened rivers of preaching, 582. The different ages of the Church are counted according to the measure of preaching, 613. At the end of the world the Church will receive many children through preaching, ibid. Preaching is readily despised when the preacher’s life is unknown, 623. Doctrine delivered without order is barren and defiles, 744. Why one preaching of the word abandons some people and receives others is altogether hidden, 871. Preaching is useless without the breath of the Holy Spirit, 884. From the light of preaching blaze the ardor of charity and the heat of persecution, 935. The effects of the apostles’ preaching, ibid. When grace ceases, preaching does not pass into the heart, 938, 939. Preaching is said to resemble thunder, 938. Preaching was granted to the Gentile world, 939. The word of God is scattered in a cloud when it is announced to unbelievers, 955. Preaching that benefits some harms others, 961. How great the blessing of preaching will be in the final times, 1159. The preaching of one who appears frivolous in character is not easily accepted, 1193. Often, from a few words heard like sparks, the whole heart of the hearer catches fire, 1194. The word of preaching is seed in the heart of the hearer, ibid. The order of preaching, conversion, and reward, 1237. He speaks rightly who first does by obedience what he admonishes others to do, 1271. One part of the hearers is drenched, while another, not drenched, withers, 1272. From the preaching of repentance comes mourning, followed by the other virtues, 1274. When the doctrine received from preachers is accepted, the condition of the Church and the authority of both Testaments are raised up, 1277. As hearers progress in charity and understanding, the grace of the Spirit increases in preachers, 1278. Why preaching is withdrawn from certain people by God, 1447, 1497. The preaching of one who lives badly is despised, 1476.

The subjects of preaching must be proportionate to the capacity of the hearers, 548, 636, 639, 961. Uneducated hearers must be irrigated not by an inundation but by a gentle distillation of knowledge, 548, 635. What is perverse must first be uprooted, and then what is right must be preached, 564. The subjects of preaching must be drawn from the sacred pages, 573, 1320. The rain of strength is the preaching of Christ’s divinity; the rain of weakness is the preaching of Christ’s humanity, 874. The manner of preaching used by the righteous, 778. The preacher must speak God’s words, not his own, 1268, 1319. First let him instruct people in faith, then in a devout life, 1285. Five things must be considered by the preacher in preaching, 1286. Hearers must be instructed from the words and deeds of the holy Fathers, 1398. The learned scribe brings forth new and old things from the treasury of both Testaments, 1475. The end of preaching is not food but the fruit of future reward, 615, 1216. What it means for a preacher to speak from God and before God, 717. Under the pretext of advising, the desire to appear breaks out, 740. When God is revealed in his majesty, preaching will cease, 963. The little spheres of the lampstand signify the labor of preaching, and the lilies signify recompense, 1216. The speech of a teacher is idle if it cannot provide the fire of love, 1578. Empty glory must not be sought from the labor of preaching, 1412. To seek praise from preaching is to sell a great thing at a cheap price, ibid.

Preachers are called farmers, 726; likewise friends, 1096; and maidservants, ibid.; angels, 309, 1122; winged creatures, 1198; eagles, 1044; foundations of the Church, 901; oxen, 218, 1160, 1193. Holy preachers are called the oxen of the widow—that is, of the Church—523; and yoked oxen, 1161. The preachers of the Synagogue are called heaven, 58. Holy preachers are called heavens, 292, 869, 978, 1579, 1635. They are also called builders, 1314; and dogs of the flock, that is, of the Church, 643, 1652; coals of fire, 934; hinds—those preachers who are called hinds, 973; silver columns of the litter of our king, 1334; columns of heaven and of the Church, 550; counselors, 373; consuls, 128; ravens, in the manner in which they are called ravens, 577, 971.

Preachers are called teeth, 382; the teeth of the Church, 1104; and the teeth of the Lord, 1197; horses, 1016; rivers, 958; lightning, ibid., 1211; foundations of the Church, 899; roosters, 959. Why their loins are said to be girded, ibid. They are also called hail, 934; slingstones, 1125; [Col. 1467] locusts, 1018, 1019; the jaw of the Church, 422; physicians, 1269; mountains, 290, 578; merchants, 1096; clouds, 547, 879, 957, 1371; workers, 879. Holy preachers are called the mouth of God, 1097. The mouth of the devil is the preachers of errors, 422. Holy preachers are called the doors of the Church, 911; the feet of the Lord, which he anoints and cleanses, 615; the feet of the needy person, 578; the hoof of the calf, 1193; gates, 1329, 1403; carved gates, 1365; and the gates of Zion, 1103. They are called branches of a tree, 604; kings, 128; rivers of the Church, 1278; archers, 1124; suns, 291; watchmen, 1282; stars, 291; drops of dew, 941; the roof of the Church, 1278; and torrents, 652.

Preachers are compared with sheep that have been shorn and washed, 1104. Like rivers, preachers return to the place from which they flow so that they may flow again, 1212. They are represented by the reeds of the lampstand, 1216. A preacher must stand on high in his life, so that he may be useful through foresight, 1283. The minds of preachers are signified by jasper in the fortifications of the Church, 1365. Preachers are represented by oxen, lions, and cherubim, among crowns and plaits, 1414. Preachers are signified by the servant who calls the invited guests to dinner, 1620; and by the Egyptian servant despised by his Amalekite master and cast aside on the road, 1622.

How effective the example of a preacher is, 685. Most people who were harsh persecutors become great preachers, 878, 997. Why preachers are said to have their loins girded, 959. Preachers should make their teaching agree with their life, 976. Preachers receive life and doctrine from God, 1016. The activity of a preacher without speech that stirs others does not benefit them, ibid. In a preacher, speech must be joined with the strength of action, 1017. Unless speech and life agree in a preacher, the power of perfection will not appear, 1016. The perfection of preachers is expressed by locusts, 1018. At one time they leap up to contemplation, and at another rebound to the active life, ibid. The life of preachers must be examined like coin, 1111. The life of preachers must agree with the institutions of the ancient Fathers, ibid. A preacher must have mature age, 1183. The character of a preacher, 1193. The twofold life of preachers, 1195. Preachers never turn back, because they always strive toward better things, 1198. For preaching, the consciousness of holy love builds up more than practice in speaking, 1268. Preachers must be taken up by the Spirit of God and lifted above earthly things, 1273. A preacher must stand on high in his life, so that he may be useful through foresight, 1283. The preacher’s life must be elevated and watchful, 1284. Let him burn so that he may set others ablaze, ibid. Those who go out to preach must afterward return to themselves, 1295, and be enclosed within the inner chambers of conscience, 1296. The figure of preachers is Noah, 1344. What the excellence of the order of preachers is, 1345. Preachers must far surpass their hearers, 1367. The glory of a preacher is the progress of the hearer, 1377. A preacher must do great things in such a way that he does not neglect small ones, 1410. What rule of discipline a preacher must observe, 1414. Neither must his strictness be excessive nor his mercy too lax, ibid. Preachers must love their neighbors perfectly and therefore desire nothing in this world, 1452, 1498. Every faithful person in his own household ought to perform the office of a preacher, 1396, 1500.

A preacher must imitate the manner of a river, 4. Among the sons of Job celebrating banquets, who are to be understood as preachers, 26. [Col. 1468] Hearers must be nourished according to the measure of their understanding, ibid., 549, 636. These are signified by Job’s daughters, ibid. How stains contracted by preachers are to be washed away, 27. Conscience does not hinder the speaker when life precedes the tongue, 206. Preachers should devote themselves to the active and contemplative life, buried in a double tomb, 207. The cause of the preachers’ groaning is their desire for delayed blessedness, 218. Preachers ought to do what they say, 374, 609, 976, 734. Which preacher ought to rebuke faults, 419. The preacher is placed here as a sign against his enemy, 424. Preachers ought to preach heavenly rather than earthly things in moderation, 548. The preacher must consider the capacity of the hearer, 549. The preacher must first uproot harmful things from his hearers and afterward plant useful ones, 564. The preacher must draw the origins of causes from the sacred pages, 573. A law has been imposed upon preachers themselves, 609. When a preacher is despised, he should be silent and flee to the mud of repentance, 676. A preacher should be silent unless he can benefit others by speaking, 716. How he may know that he will benefit his hearers, ibid. A preacher must strive not only to speak well but also, by living, to adorn what he says well, 734, 1411. What it means for a preacher to place an iron frying pan between himself and his hearers, 816. What it means to build fortifications, ibid. Preachers not only point out the vices that storm the mind but also those virtues that strengthen it, ibid. Those who rouse the minds of hearers to attention, 831. The care of preachers for their subjects, 880. God directs his preachers as he wishes, ibid. The force of waters covers preachers when unbelievers rage against them, 956. Preachers must not attribute the progress of their hearers to themselves but to God, 958. When the work of their mission is completed, they must return to the secrecy of contemplation, ibid. A preacher must keep vigilant over himself and call the sleeping to vigils, 962. Preachers receive from God what enables them to perform their office worthily, 963. Those who proceed to spiritual war under Christ their leader must show by their deeds what they announce with their mouths, 991. The preacher’s office is to dig out earthly thoughts from his hearers, 1020. Disregarding the efforts of the enemy, the devout preacher continually labors for the conversion of sinners, 1026. He anticipates the enemy’s ambushes and tricks in the hearts of others, 1031. He heals the wounds of his own weakness in such a way that he does not neglect those of others, 1032. Eagles fly to the corpse—that is, preachers hungry for the salvation of sinners, 1044. Preachers are silent while mourning amid reprobate minds, 1081. The work of preachers, 1096. Why preachers are sent two by two, 1161. One must return from public speech to the court of the heart, 1168. The qualities of preachers, 1190, 1254, 1366, 1411. Preachers are sent into the four regions of the world, 1195. They ought to travel through various places, 1209. Who go and return, 1211. Like lightning, they shake, terrify, illumine, and kindle the minds of those who behold them, ibid. The office of preaching must not be given to the weak, 1251. One who has authority in the word should speak rightly and freely if he presides; if he is subordinate, he should humbly suggest what is good, 1254. When preachers are silent, the food of life is denied, 1260. Whoever opens his mouth draws in the spirit, ibid. The preacher is told: “Eat and feed,” and so forth, 1265. The office of the preacher, 1268, 1285. So that he may please his hearers, the preacher composes something by lying, speaks his own words and not God’s, 1268. He must first open his ear to God before opening his mouth to the people, 1284. The preacher will be guilty of the blood of the righteous person who falls [Col. 1469] if he remains silent, 1288. The righteous …

The preacher is also bound to admonish, 1289. Because of bad hearers, speech is denied to good teachers, 1298. Whoever has advanced in understanding spiritual things should offer them to others, 1321. It belongs to preachers to cut branches from the trees and lay them in the way for Christ, 1352. When a preacher is called learned, 1474. Preachers prepare the way for Christ, 1496. Few properly fulfill this office, ibid. Because of the fault either of preachers or of hearers, the word of preaching is withdrawn, 1497. Whoever undertakes the office of preaching must be free from greed, 1498. A preacher must have great trust in God, ibid. What it means for a preacher, while on the way, to greet no one, ibid. A preacher must flee the burden of secular affairs, ibid. He must not fortify himself by the example of others who act foolishly, ibid. Peace offered by a preacher is never without effect, ibid. Whoever cannot benefit many should at least strive to benefit a few, 1530.

—A preacher is not heard by a reprobate heart, 370, 955. The preacher’s shame: when those hearing do not receive the words of life that he preaches, 447. The ministry of the voice is empty when God does not inwardly give increase, 545. The preacher who separates the precious from the vile, 583. The voice penetrates the hearer’s heart if the work is brought to completion that has sounded from the mouth, 610. What is taught with authority is first practiced and only afterward spoken, 742. The words of preachers are like nails, 779. Preachers first terrify and afterward console, 862. At Christ’s command preachers are sent to certain parts of the world, but are rejected by others, 900. A preacher can give words to the ears, but cannot open the heart, 939. The flashes go forth when preachers perform wondrous works; they return when they attribute everything to the power of their author, 958. The adaptability of preachers toward everyone, 961. Preachers are like women in laboring spiritually: what pains and what gifts they have, 975. The measure of the fruit follows the measure of virtues, 977. Preachers cannot beget spiritually except by weeping, ibid. Their children go to the pasture of eternal greenness, 978. What preacher digs the earth, 1021. A military form must be observed by preachers, 1024. Only those who would not be suitable in themselves are selected for preaching the Gospel, 1096. If a preacher wishes to be heard willingly, he should sympathize with his hearers, 1281. The preacher’s speech is fivefold, 1286. The voices of preachers are compared with glowing air, 1194. The words of preachers are called sparks, ibid. The word of teaching is especially granted for the advancement of both teachers and hearers, 1298. Preachers who set virtues against vices point them out, 1303. Preachers establish camps and fortifications against the ambushes of demons, ibid. Hearers advance through the teaching of preachers, and preachers through the life of their hearers, 1366. Preachers are ashamed not to observe what they teach, ibid. How much teachers ought to excel their hearers, 1367. Hearers are thereby urged toward humility, ibid. The preacher’s glory is the hearer’s progress, 1377. What are the good qualities of a hearer, 1396. The voice of preachers is withdrawn because of the fault of subjects, 1497. Preachers should have tongues of fire, 1578. The preacher’s tongue heals the wounds of our mind, 1652.

—Christ cleanses the hearts of his preachers, 27. The humility of the preacher who considers himself an unprofitable servant, 545. The preacher does not seek a gift but looks for fruit, 615. He flees honor because of pride, but wishes to be honored for the usefulness of preaching [Col. 1469], 623. He should proclaim humility, the mother of virtues, more by his conduct than by his words, 742. What preachers must consider in order to flee pride, ibid., 1366. The power of the preachers’ faith, 862. The study of contemplation is necessary for preachers, 959. Discernment is especially necessary for a preacher, 961, 976, 1284, 1286. He knows how to speak rightly who knows how to keep silence in an orderly way, 968. Those who prepare themselves to preach should first renew themselves inwardly through virtues, 976. How great are the labors of preachers, 977. What caution preachers must exercise, ibid. Preachers ought to be sober-minded, 978. Preachers of the faith have benefited more by their death than by their voice, 991. The place of humility in a preacher, 994, 1298. The preacher is raised to the summit of perfection when he is strengthened not only by the active but also by the contemplative life, 1018. In the peace of the Church, preachers should be humble; in persecution, upright and brave, 1019. When they suffer adversity outwardly, they inwardly smell the wonders of eternal blessedness, ibid. The preacher’s security is compared with the lion, the strongest of beasts, 1022. The preacher’s weakness must be strong, his punishment victorious, and his patience dominant, 1027. The strong preacher is not frightened by the danger of battle, because he rejoices in the triumph of victory, ibid. The preacher’s sorrow arises from the hardness of his hearers, and his joy from their conversion, 1155. The holy preacher ought to imitate Christ’s virtues, 1191. Good works should accompany the faith and contemplation of preachers, 1193. Holy preachers should possess the gravity of life together with courage and discernment, ibid. Sound and ardor are fitting for preachers, 1194. The virtue and wisdom of holy preachers are joined together in charity, 1198. The flower of the grape signifies the preacher’s virtue and reputation, 1214. We must first fulfill God’s commands before teaching our neighbors rightly, 1270. The humble preacher alone divides the waters in the streets, 1296. The preacher should humble himself because of his weaknesses and groan, 1297. How necessary the preacher’s zeal is, even if it causes pain, 1304. Armed with this, he will escape divine judgment, ibid. What the preacher receives from God he owes to his hearers, 1319. How one who teaches others ought to fight against pride, 1366. And against anger, ibid. How great a danger threatens the preacher from the applause of his hearers, 1412. How great must be the preacher’s discernment between discipline and mercy, 1414. The preacher’s office must not be undertaken without love of neighbor, 1496. Trust in God is necessary for a preacher, 1498. The virtues of preachers are the adornments of heaven, 1579. In bodily affliction the preacher should carry the cross of the flesh, and in compassion for his neighbor the cross of the mind, 1588.

—Preachers must beware of vain joy, 27, 304. Preachers who love temporal things abandon the truth, 375. To what foolish end a preacher is brought, 373. When persecution presses, the weak fear preaching the truth, 423. A preacher scarcely avoids sins by preaching, 615. Who are those who adulterate the word of God, 716. A preacher must beware of exalting himself through the fault of pride, 734, 1296, 1366. A preacher must be free from vices, 741. Some pretend to modesty, 743. They falsely boast of simplicity, ibid. If a preacher is more concerned with bodily care than with preaching, his condemnation is to be feared, 991. Preachers must beware of the things they censure, 1260. The food of life is denied to those who are silent, ibid. Preachers who hunt after empty glory sell a great thing for a paltry price [Col. 1470], 1412. Stipends are owed to preachers, 615. Feet are washed with butter when hearers provide the stipends owed to holy preachers, ibid. Temporal stipends are established for preaching, 1498. The very means of sustenance are already the payment for the work, 1499. There are two payments for preaching: one on the way, the other in the homeland, ibid. The former must serve the latter, ibid. Whoever preaches for an earthly payment deprives himself of the eternal one, ibid. Pastors who consume the sins of the people, ibid. A discerning pastor spends the talent of the word so that he may not take the stipend of food to his own condemnation, 1500.

—Good pastors preserve by living what they say, 244, 1411. Who is the perfect preacher, 207. Good preachers do not fear being mocked while teaching what is right, 485. In their words they seek to benefit both their hearers and themselves, ibid. They do not devote preaching for the sake of livelihood, but receive livelihood for the sake of preaching, 615. Good preachers do not rejoice in the gift of possessions but in the fruit of those who give them, ibid. In times of persecution, the good are more ready to die than to be silent, 665. Prudent preachers diligently watch over the fruit of preaching, 675. They sow upon all waters, 685. A faithful preacher envies no one but wishes the truth to sound from everyone’s mouth, 686. Good preachers speak from God and before God, 717. What is the office of a good preacher, 734. The image of the best preacher, ibid. A good preacher preserves leisure for silence by his vow, but exercises the office of speech in his ministry, ibid. It is part of a good preacher’s duty not to display his wisdom but to restrain others from error, 739. Inflamed by the zeal of charity, he preaches lest by his silence he become a participant in the sins of the wrongdoers, 740. Holy preachers speak from the root of humility so that they may bear the fruit of piety, 778. When they are about to correct others, they first offer soothing words, 779. Like skilled physicians, they first feel the wound and afterward strike, 780. What it signifies that a holy preacher builds fortifications and carries up a rampart, 816, 1303. Good preachers are signified by the stars of rain, 857. God calls peoples to faith and repentance through the words and miracles of preachers, 862. Good preachers both terrify and feed peoples, ibid. Holy preachers, whose manner of life is in heaven, accommodate themselves to their weak brothers, 873. Winter is the present life, in which the rains of holy preachers abound, 874. Holy preachers wish to exhort certain people but cannot, 879. They survey everything, with God directing their course, ibid., and regulating their movements, 880, 882, 900. Inspired by God, holy preachers water and give light, 881. From the harmony of teachers and hearers, mutual charity burns within them, 883. Teachers should attribute the progress of their hearers not to themselves but to the Holy Spirit, 884. Holy preachers are gates set against the raging sea: they are battered by the waves but cannot be broken through, 911. These gates are open to the humble and closed to the proud, 912. As persecution increased, so did the ardor of holy preachers, 938. They go forth from God and return to him, 957, 1211. They strike their adversaries with words and protect themselves with miracles, 958. They are given understanding so that what the tongue speaks may be alive in the conscience, 960. They must not, while themselves sluggish in action, rouse others with their voice, 963. The harmonious speech of preachers is signified by the concert of heaven [Col. 1471], 964. Holy preachers are young stags, 969. They know that by their own strength they can do nothing, ibid. They burn with zeal to win souls, ibid. They imitate their teacher Paul, 970. What it means for holy preachers, like ibexes, to catch themselves as they fall upon their own horns, 972. Why they are called hinds, 973. They sow in tears so that they may reap in joy, 977. Unless they bent down to human weakness, they would not beget children in the faith, ibid. A preacher should receive from God the strength of a horse, so that he may act rightly, and its neighing, so that he may teach rightly, 1016. Despising the assault of persecution, they know how to meet it bravely but not rashly, 1024. Once defeated, enemies resort in vain to plots against the holy preacher, 1025. Holy preachers do not cease preaching because of persecutions, 1026. They proceed from threats to open punishments, ibid. A spear is brandished with which the holy man is struck; a shield is held up by the persecutor so that he may not be heard, ibid. Who the holy preachers are who raise a standard over the darkened mountain, 1075. Holy preachers are terrified and purified by the fall and punishment of the angels, 1122. Holy preachers must imitate Christ’s virtues, 1190. Why the words of preachers are called sparks, 1194. The Lord’s darts are the words of the saints, 1211. Good preachers learn through love what they proclaim by teaching, 1212. What the sound of wings in preachers and of waters in converts signifies, 1236. Preachers must not fear the cruelty or threats of the wicked, 1253. Love teaches the preacher to speak gently about God, 1267. Preachers must be taken up by God’s Spirit and raised above earthly things, 1273. They are raised by knowledge and taken up by their life, 1279. Whoever still finds the present life sweet has not been raised and taken up, ibid. A preacher should consider what, to whom, when, in what manner, and how much he should say, 1286. He should imitate the farmer, who adapts seeds to the soils, 1288. When it is fitting for a preacher to keep silent, 1297. When it is necessary to press rebellious people against the truth, ibid. Whoever lives and preaches rightly is a treasury in the house of God, 1364. Tables are constructed from squared stones, signifying the virtues of holy preachers set forth for imitation, 1406. A good preacher is both chariot and charioteer, 1412.

—Preachers of the Jews are called oxen pressed under the yoke of the Law, 25. The wicked person who understands and says what is right has a harvest for others to eat, 185. Whoever devotes himself to sacred learning with an eye to temporal payment does not persevere in the good he had begun, 274. The preaching of a hypocrite is fruitless, 276, 609. God grants the word of truth to those who practice it and takes it away from those who do not, 374. Why bad preachers are called vessels of papyrus, 422. The strength of a perverse preacher is an exalted knowledge of speech, 536. The preacher of the world’s error is joined to the rich, ibid. Such a perverse preacher will endure as long as he lives in the body, ibid. The bad preacher sows while fasting and another eats, when he does not practice what he teaches, 685. His offspring is the one who is uprooted, 686. Having lost his own children, he envies the life of others’ children, ibid. Those who serve empty glory by preaching what is right are not reconciled but are often condemned, 733. Proud preachers are signified by Elihu, his father, and his kin, 735. They attack heretics by preaching what is right, and the Church by their pride, ibid. While rebuking those who err, they wish to display their own wisdom rather than benefit others [Col. 1471], 739. It is characteristic of the arrogant to display his knowledge, ibid. The proud imitate in good preachers the loftiness of their speech, not their intention of being useful, 740. The proud do not preach sound doctrine soundly, because they become insolent, 742. The bad preacher vainly exalts himself over small matters, whereas the good thinks humbly of great ones, 745. Bad preachers speak what is right forcefully but do not know how to live according to what they say, 746. The proud customarily mix empty and swollen claims with true and mystical things, 777. The proud do not seek to make their hearers wise but to display their own wisdom, 778. Arrogant preachers rebuke more from anger than from charity, 779. At times they put on an appearance of humility, but it is feigned, ibid. They accuse the just of false crimes, ibid. They always wish to find things with which to strike through reproach, ibid. From the proud man’s true statements one should take what is useful and reject what is harmful, 853. Those who preach rightly but do not live rightly become heralds of their own condemnation, 887.
